newsitem.title: JAPAN: Pace of decline in Japan c/a surplus slowing - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Pace of decline in Japan c/a surplus slowing - MOF.

text.p: The pace of decline in Japan's current account surplus is slowing down, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official said on Monday.

Although current account figures will be affected by currency rates, oil prices and economic conditions both at home and abroad, growth in imports continues to exceed that of exports and the services deficit continues to grow, the official told reporters.
Meanwhile, the surplus in the income balance continues to grow, he said. "The tempo of the decline in the current account surplus is slowing down," he said.
The official was speaking after the release of current account data for February and data on Japan's trade surplus for the first 20 days of March.
The current account surplus rose 15.4 percent in February to 865.2 billion yen while the surplus in merchandise trade alone rose 2.9 percent to 878 billion yen.

Asked about the rise in the merchandise trade surplus, which was the first in 27 months, the official said he did not think there had been a drastic change in the trend and he said the trade surplus was still declining overall, although at a slower pace.
The official pointed out that Japan's trade surplus for the first 20 days of March fell 33.8 percent from a year ago to 337.48 billion yen.
Although the weaker yen tends to boost exports, structural changes such as Japanese companies shifting their production overseas continue to support growth in imports, the official said.
